$what: Provenance of aurora-effects-scene.schema.json, empyrean's CONTRACT schema, vendored into Aurora beside the codec that validates against it. scene.ts imports the .json directly; this sidecar records where those bytes came from, and test/formats/effects-schema-drift.test.ts reads `empyrean.blob` from here as its pin of record.
$why_a_sidecar_and_not_only_a_test_const: Until 2026-08-29 the pinned blob hash lived as a `const PINNED_BLOB` in effects-schema-drift.test.ts and as prose in scene.ts's header and in effects-scene-golden.test.ts's header. Three copies, one of which (scene.ts) had already gone THREE re-pins stale without anything going red, because nothing hashes a comment. The hash now lives HERE, once, and the test reads it. The prose citations remain prose and say so.
$why_vendored: Aurora's core must validate from a lone clone, inside a git worktree (where ../../empyrean is not where it is from master), and in a packaged Electron build that ships no sibling repo. A path-probe design would degrade to 'schema not found -> skip validation', which is the loud-on-unmeasurable failure this suite is not allowed to have. The cost of vendoring is staleness; the drift gate and the currency check below are the payment. See docs/reviews/2026-08-28-golden-live-tree.md for the defect that made reading a peer's LIVE WORKING TREE unacceptable, this file is never read from ../empyrean at runtime or at test time by path, only through git objects at a named revision.
$why_not_under_test_fixtures: This is a SOURCE file the app imports, not a test fixture, so it lives beside its consumer. It is also deliberately outside test/fixtures/ because the published-revision sweep in test/formats/aeon-fixture-currency.test.ts walks that tree and reads every 40-hex on a `revision*` key as an AEON revision; an empyrean SHA sitting there would be checked for reachability from aeon's master and fail for a reason that has nothing to do with it.

what_changed_at_this_pin.semantic: ONE KEY RETYPED, TWO DESCRIPTIONS CORRECTED. A parsed leaf diff run HERE, not taken from the sending lane, found 294 leaves before and 293 after: 1 added (/$defs/layer/properties/rowRemap/oneOf/1/properties/height_shift/enum/0 = 4), 2 removed (that node's minimum 3 and maximum 7), and 2 changed in place (the same branch's plane_y and height_shift descriptions). No other key, type, range or $ref moved. The text diff is ONE hunk, 4 lines out for 3 in, every other byte identical, so the sending lane's "formatting preserved, 7 lines" holds as stated.
what_changed_at_this_pin.why: height_shift admitted 3..7 while aeon can generate exactly one ladder, row_remap_ladder16(), so four of the five legal values were a legal document and a red build. aeon refused them inside its own tool (aeon c1579f6e) — a writer-binding rule no consumer could read. The hub moved the refusal into the contract where a consumer can see it. It is an ENUM and not a const on this lane's objection: an enum IS the buildable set, so it widens one entry at a time by amendment and Aurora's picker grows with no Aurora edit, which a const cannot express.
what_changed_at_this_pin.parser_impact: LARGE, AND LOUD, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS SAFE. scene-ui.ts derived height_shift's picker through boundsAt(), which reads minimum/maximum and THROWS when they are absent — measured, not argued: vendoring these bytes with no code change took 71 test files down at import and dropped 1,640 tests out of the run entirely. There was no silently-wrong path. The repair is admittedIntegers() in scene-ui.ts, which serves an enum, a const and a minimum/maximum range alike; EFFECTS_ROW_REMAP_HEIGHT_SHIFTS is now the primary derivation and EFFECTS_ROW_REMAP_HEIGHT_SHIFT_BOUNDS is derived from it (the ENDS, never membership — a sparse enum would make those different questions). EFFECTS_ROW_REMAP_BUILDABLE_SHIFT reads null because the description dropped its "TODAY ONLY n BUILDS" clause, which is its documented self-retirement firing: every buildability warning went quiet with no consumer edit. The two amended descriptions ARE read by parsers here — the buildable-shift clause and, in the plane_y case, by Aurora prose that claimed sole enforcement of the 511 ceiling and no longer may.
